audit.why: HARD, 42.14% over 2105 games — Mel's worst-style matchup: nothing in his basic combo is reflectable, E dodges her snare and execute, and post-6 one shark deletes her. Rating 8/10 fits the data.

audit.whatIsWrong: Total layer disagreement: full phases[0-6].side all Fizz, content win[0-6] all Mel (packet chart also all Mel, which its own defect note flags as contradicting the 42.14% WR). Full whys 0-3 describe Mel winning under a Fizz side; content whys 4-6 claim Mel holds the edge at 6/first item/late while its own spikes call the shark combo lethal.
audit.why: Kit-grounded split: levels 1-3ish melee Fizz must walk into 950-range volleys with no kill threat (Mel); from 6, Chum the Waters guarantees the combo and with ignite kills outright — the page's own spikes[1] calls R 'the whole matchup' — and first item/late keep that threat (Fizz).
audit.corrected: Chart set Mel 0-3 / Fizz 4-6 on BOTH layers, whys rewritten on every flipped row.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were tradeGood/tradeBad verbatim; reflect scope unstated (only the R fish is a projectile; Q dash and E hop are not); W Seastone Trident auto-reset tell (missing interaction) unstated.
audit.why: Kit: E 16s-8s untargetable hop (dodges snare, volley, and the R strike); Q 8s-6s 550-range dash; W 7s-3s empowered-attack auto reset; R 120s projectile fish, grounding+knockup.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — the execute threshold turns your chip war into a countdown he can see.
edits.after: Chum the Waters guarantees the combo — the shark plus ignite kills you from full; never sit low at 6.

edits.before: Luden's spike: snare-volley chunks half bars and the execute cleans the remainder. Force contacts.
edits.after: His first item makes the R combo lethal and E roams snowball sides — shove and cross-map, don't duel.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: One landed shark still deletes you late — fight with peel, snare his landing, and never facecheck brush.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Playful/Trickster (E): 16s at rank 1, 8 at max — the untargetable hop dodges your snare, your volley, even the R strike; bait it before spending burst. - Urchin Strike (Q): 8s dash, not reflectable. - Chum the Waters: 120s — only the thrown fish is a projectile Rebuttal blocks.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Rebuttal's immunity and move speed let you survive the Q-W opener even at melee range — glow, walk out, and his bleed hits nothing.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Urchin Strike and the hop aren't projectiles — Rebuttal blocks the thrown shark, but his whole basic combo goes straight through the glow.

edits.before: At 5 he still lacks R, so your poke and zone control stay ahead.
edits.after: At 6 Chum the Waters guarantees his combo — one shark kills you.

edits.before: You keep out-ranging and out-clearing Fizz on the lane through first item.
edits.after: His first-item spike makes the R combo lethal and his roams snowball.

edits.before: Your superior range and waveclear hold the lane edge into the late game.
edits.after: One landed R deletes you late — he dictates every fight you must join.

notes: The two layers disagreed on all seven rows (full all-Fizz, content all-Mel). Resolved to Mel 0-3 / Fizz 4-6: pre-6 poke dominance is kit-grounded and both layers' whys describe it; post-6 the page's own spikes call the R combo lethal and the 42.14% WR supports Fizz. Confidence Medium on rows 2-3 (Fizz has full combo from 3, but no reliable kill without R). Fizz W auto-reset wind-up tell (missing interaction) had no natural in-band home outside report[] — recorded here, not invented. Rebuttal-vs-shark: R carries the projectile flag so the fish toss is blockable; the erupting shark after attach is presumably not — phrased edits around the toss only.
